challenge.better_approach: Stubbing cli._announce_seals whole would also do it, but reach is the narrower seam and keeps the announce code running under the proof; the orchestrator named reach or the published scratch bus.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the only live contact in this proof is _announce_seals; a grep of cli.main --seal for other bus calls is part of the build.
challenge.prior_art: 9dbac8691def's proof patches cairn.tools.bus_client.reach the same way; cff5a197b3c4 uses scratch_bus. Neither touches this proof.
challenge.real_collision: None: the proof belongs to the tester component and its ticket d5a05b6d1752's teeth are kept unchanged.

answers.falsifier: Done: with CAIRN_BUS_HOME at an unanswering far address, the proof's seal teeth are green and print no announce failure. Wrong: the red was not the bus, and the teeth stay red with the bus stubbed.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator measured it on ticket 9dbac8691def (CairnCommons/tickets/): cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_reseal_names_the_tickets_whose_hollow_it_voids.py sealed red while akiendelllinux.local:7419 refused connections, and green once it answered
answers.how: In the proof's _seal, monkeypatch cairn.tools.bus_client.reach to a quiet stub bus (post, flush, undelivered) so cli.main --seal's _announce_seals never reaches the live bus; a new tooth points CAIRN_BUS_HOME at a far address nobody answers and asserts the seal still runs clean.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (a fake red is a hollow measurement: the proof measured the LAN, not its subject) and Law 3; outline 9.4.2.3.3 (a seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged).
answers.what: The reseal-names-the-voided-hollow proof seals the same verdict whether or not a live far bus answers, because its seal runs never post to a live bus.

bullets.text: A proof that drives cli.main --seal reaches the live bus through _announce_seals; on a far home a down LAN bus turns its seal red (measured 2026-11-13).
